title: Holiness
lead: To be holy (qadosh) is to be set apart for God, who is holy above all (Isaiah 6:3). The Bible traces holiness from the seventh day and the holy mountain through the tabernacle, priests and Israel's call, "You will be holy, because I am holy" (Leviticus 19:2), to the church as a holy temple (1 Peter 1:15–16; 1 Corinthians 3:16–17).

sections.b: The first thing called holy is a day, the seventh (Genesis 2:3). Ground becomes holy where God appears (Exodus 3:5), and Israel is called a holy nation (Exodus 19:6). Leviticus 17–26, often called the Holiness Code, repeats the command "You will be holy, because I am holy, I the LORD your God" (Leviticus 19:2) and applies it to food, sex, justice and care for the poor. Isaiah's vision of the thrice-holy God (Isaiah 6:3) makes "the Holy One of Israel" his favorite name for God. Zechariah pictures a day when even cooking pots will be holy (Zechariah 14:20–21). In the New Testament believers are called "holy ones" (saints), the church is God's holy temple (1 Corinthians 3:16–17), and 1 Peter 1:15–16 repeats Leviticus' call. Revelation's living creatures still cry "holy, holy, holy" (Revelation 4:8).
